etymologies.etymologyHTML: Unadapted borrowing from French souvenir (literally “memory”); compare memento.

definitions.definition: An item of sentimental value, that is given or kept to remember an event or location.

quote.text: Back then, nobody knew in the schoolyardNow then, you have grown up to be this hardGo then, walk through this world with your heart scarredYou're the souvenir of sadness

quote.citation: 2005, Steven Church, Guinness Book of Me, Simon and Schuster, →ISBN, page 138:
quote.text: The tourists stuck to the safe confines of the gift shop, where they bought souvenir combs, shot glasses, oversize pencils, and blocks of cedar painted with rhyming poems and shellacked to a high gloss.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To take (something) as a souvenir, especially illicitly, for example during wartime.

quote.citation: 1979, Gustav Hasford, The Short-Timers, New York: Bantam Books, published 1980, →ISBN, page 57:
quote.text: "Doubletime up to the ville and souvenir me one cute orphan, man, but be sure you get a dirty one, a really skuzzy one."

quote.citation: 2017, Fiona Farrell, Decline and Fall on Savage Street, →ISBN, page 84:
quote.text: The word is they're waiting for some blokes who had gone off souveniring before the order was announced.
